paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu said coldly, “It is still too early to rejoice!”

units.source_en: Ieyasu said coldly, “It is still too early to rejoice!”

paragraphs.source_en: “We have only reached Kiyosu. To reach Osaka, we must still pass through Mino and Ōmi. Beyond them lies the battlefield, and Yamashiro, Yamato, Izumi, and Kawachi are all enemy territory.”

paragraphs.source_en: Naokatsu stared in astonishment and scratched at his temple. Ieyasu’s face was calm, without the slightest excitement; perhaps he felt that he had merely received what was rightfully due.

paragraphs.source_en: “Hideyasu, do you not resent Uesugi?”

units.source_en: “Hideyasu, do you not resent Uesugi?”
units.source_zh: “秀康，你不厌上杉？”

paragraphs.source_zh: “秀康，你不厌上杉？”

units.source_en: “Father!”

paragraphs.source_zh: “父亲大人！”

paragraphs.source_en: “Do not be hasty. You must think this through carefully. The man must possess sufficient authority and be capable of matching the enemy in battle at any time. With such a man stationed here, Kagekatsu’s will to fight would be greatly diminished. Kagekatsu has never been greatly ambitious; unlike Ishida, he does not covet the realm, nor will he come forth of his own accord to provoke us.”

units.source_en: “But…”

paragraphs.source_en: Hideyasu stared fixedly at his father, filled with admiration—his father had long since decided that he would remain behind to guard Edo. He declared loudly, “Father, Hideyasu is willing to remain here. So long as Hideyasu stands here, Kagekatsu shall not pass!”

units.source_en: Hideyasu stared fixedly at his father, filled with admiration—his father had long since decided that he would remain behind to guard Edo.

paragraphs.source_en: Utsunomiya’s main castle would be defended by Hideyasu and Gamō Hideyuki, the second defensive castle entrusted to the seasoned Ogasawara Hidemasa, and the third to Satomi Yoshiyasu, for a combined force of roughly twenty thousand men.

paragraphs.source_en: Thus the defense of the east was settled. All that remained was to decide when the former Toyotomi retainers would break camp. Ieyasu fixed the time at noon on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month. Before then, the commanders would meet one last time at Oyama and afterward march directly west.

paragraphs.source_en: Every preparation for the western campaign was complete, yet Ieyasu showed no sign of departing from Oyama. Heavy rain continued from the twenty-eighth through the twenty-ninth, forcing the generals to make their separate ways back through the mud.

paragraphs.source_en: After calmly seeing the generals off, Ieyasu once more turned his close attention to Kagekatsu—or, more precisely, began watching the movements of Naoe Kanetsugu and Satake Yoshinobu. Though every measure for dealing with the two men was already in place, whether they would prematurely widen the present upheaval was a matter of immense consequence.

paragraphs.source_en: Only on the morning of the fourth day of the eighth month did Ieyasu depart Oyama. He traveled upstream toward Koga in a small boat, had Kurihashi cut off, and then headed straight for Edo with an escort of only five or six small craft.
